headline: Chile Eliminates Dog-Transmitted Rabies as Public Health Threat
meta_description: Chile becomes the first South American country validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, marking a major public health victory.
summary_short: Chile has achieved a major milestone by becoming the first country in South America to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem.
body:
Chile has become the first country in South America to be validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem—a landmark achievement in disease control on the continent.

The validation represents years of sustained effort to interrupt transmission of the virus through domestic dog populations, one of the primary sources of human rabies exposure in the region. This success in Chile sets a new benchmark for other South American nations working toward similar goals.

Rabies remains a serious global threat, but progress in controlling it through animal vaccination programs and public health infrastructure demonstrates what focused regional commitment can achieve. Chile's recognition as rabies-free in this category reflects both rigorous epidemiological standards and the country's dedication to protecting its population from this fatal disease.
quick_facts: First South American country validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies
Dog-transmitted rabies no longer a public health problem in Chile
Achievement follows sustained disease control efforts in the region
